content:
The test image shows a tomato stem at/near soil level with:
- White cottony/fluffy mycelial growth on the stem
- Small, dark, round sclerotia embedded in the white mycelium
- Stem rot at the soil line

This pattern is classic for Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii) — white mycelium + small round sclerotia at the stem base. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference confirms white mycelial growth at the stem base typical of Southern Blight. The test image matches well: white cottony mycelium on the stem at soil level, with the highly diagnostic small, round, black sclerotia (mustard-seed sized) embedded in the mycelium — the hallmark of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight).

Sclerotinia Timber Rot is ruled out because its sclerotia are larger and irregularly elongated (rat-dropping shaped), not small and round.
